findings.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope, allowing administrators with only realm-wide group-view permission to create or modify groups

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authorization resource internal IDs instead of actual group IDs, causing incorrect user searches and counts for group-based member permissions

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope, allowing administrators with only realm-wide group-view permission to create or modify groups
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly accepts VIEW scope, which would allow users with only VIEW permission to perform management/write operations (create or modify groups) that they should not have access to. Both comments point to the same security bug where canManage() should only check for MANAGE scope, not VIEW.

This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authorization resource internal IDs instead of actual group IDs, causing incorrect user searches and counts for group-based member permissions
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same core problem as the golden comment: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is returning/using authorization resource internal IDs instead of actual group IDs, which causes incorrect behavior for user searches and counts. The golden comment explains this in more detail (hasPermission resolves by name, groupResource.getId() is being added to granted, mismatch with JPA queries and interface contract), but both are pointing to the same fundamental bug - the method is operating on resource IDs rather than the underlying group IDs it should be using.
